grading: One point per explicitly requested criterion fully supported by the answer. Omissions or contradictions score zero; relevant quotations count. The frozen key is identical before and after. Manual grader identity and limitations are reported.

questions.question: How does split_nv decide where positional arguments stop and name-value pairs begin? Explain the positional limit, recognition of a name before that limit, and case handling in the returned names.
criteria: Positional scanning stops at the earlier of the input length and npos unless a name-value start is recognized first.
A recognized start must be text whose lowercased value matches a declared name and must have a following value.
Name matching is case-insensitive, and returned pair names use the spelling from the declared names list.

questions.question: For name-value arguments, what happens with an odd remaining argument count, an unknown name, and repeated valid names? Explain what nv_get returns for repeats, including copying.
criteria: An odd remaining count raises the invalid argument list error with identifier MATLAB:TooManyInputs.
An unknown textual name raises an invalid name-value argument error listing valid names, with an empty identifier.
split_nv retains repeated pairs in order; nv_get takes the last matching value and returns cp(value).

questions.question: In arg_check, does class conversion precede dimension checking? Which source classes can convert to a numeric or logical declaration? What happens when conversion raises MatlabError versus a different exception?
criteria: Class conversion is attempted before dimension checking, unless the value already has the declared class.
Numeric/logical targets accept numeric, logical and char source classes and use _convert; other source classes fail that conversion admission.
A MatlabError during conversion becomes the prefixed type-or-convertible error through _using; exceptions outside MatlabError are not caught there.

questions.question: How does arg_check compare actual and declared dimensions? Explain what None means, how ranks of different lengths are aligned, and whether a value with matching dimensions is reshaped.
criteria: None in a declared dimension is a wildcard that accepts any actual size in that position.
Actual and requested dimension lists are padded with trailing ones to their maximum length for comparison.
If all padded dimensions match or are wildcards, the value is returned without reshaping or scalar expansion.

questions.question: When arg_check finds a size mismatch, in what order does it try scalar expansion and row/column conversion? State the conditions for each and what error is produced if neither applies.
criteria: A single-element value expands first with repmat_ only when every declared dimension is fixed, not None.
Otherwise a two-dimensional row/column vector may reshape to a two-dimensional row/column request whose non-unit dimension is its element count or None.
If neither applies, it raises a prefixed Value must be of size error via _using; None dimensions print as colons.

questions.question: What does validate do with a successful thunk result, a MatlabError, and an unrelated exception? Explain positional versus name-value prefixes, identifier preservation and the _using marker.
criteria: It calls the thunk once and discards its successful return value.

A MatlabError is replaced with a new MatlabError retaining the identifier, prefixing Invalid argument at position for a numeric position or Invalid name-value argument for a string, and marking _using=True.
It catches only MatlabError; other exception types propagate without that wrapping.

questions.question: How are the mustBeFinite/mustBePositive-style predicate validators installed and evaluated? State the default accepted classes, the behavior on empty arrays, and success/failure results.
criteria: _pred_validator installs a Builtin in _B; its default class admission accepts numeric, logical and char values.
It converts with _farr and invokes/tests the predicate only for nonempty arrays; an admitted empty array succeeds.
Every element must satisfy the predicate; failure raises MatlabError with a MATLAB:validators: identifier and success returns NOVAL.

questions.question: Contrast mustBeNumeric, mustBeNumericOrLogical and mustBeReal. Which accepts logical data, and does mustBeReal reject a complex-typed array whose imaginary components are all zero?
criteria: mustBeNumeric accepts only classes recognized by _numeric_class, excluding logical.
mustBeNumericOrLogical also accepts the logical class.
mustBeReal requires _isnumlike and rejects complex arrays only when any imaginary component is nonzero; complex dtype alone does not fail.

questions.question: How does mustBeInRange interpret its bounds and options? State how bounds are converted, which flags make each endpoint exclusive, and what happens to empty values and non-text or unrecognized options.
criteria: The value uses _farr and each bound uses _scalar; endpoints are inclusive by default.
Lowercased textual exclusive excludes both endpoints; exclude-lower and exclude-upper exclude their respective endpoints.
Empty value arrays bypass the final failure check; non-text options are filtered out and unrecognized textual options have no effect.

questions.question: Compare the accepted representations in mustBeText, mustBeTextScalar and mustBeNonzeroLengthText. Include character-array shape, string arrays and cell arrays, and identify which validator actually requires nonempty text.
criteria: mustBeText accepts Char, Str, StrArr, or a Cell containing only Char elements; it does not require nonempty text.
mustBeTextScalar accepts Str or Char with first dimension at most one; StrArr and Cell are not accepted by that check.
mustBeNonzeroLengthText accepts a nonempty Str, a Char with nonzero array size, or a nonempty Cell of nonempty Char elements; it does not accept StrArr.
